headline: Predators, Capitals claim players on NHL waivers on Oct. 24
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Nashville claimed defenseman Daemon Hunt off waivers from Minnesota, while Washington claimed St. Ivany from Winnipeg.

Hunt is a depth add with a thin track record. He was a second-round pick (65th overall) by the Wild in 2020, and he has no points in 11 games so far this season. His own expected goals, which measure the quality of the chances he's generated, are 0.61, so the lack of scoring isn't pure bad luck. The bigger concern is his 5-on-5 share of expected goals of 40.88 percent, and Minnesota has been about 19.64 percentage points better with him off the ice so far this season. That is a small sample, but it fits a player who has yet to prove he can drive play.

For Nashville, the fit is clear. The Predators sit at 3-3-4 with a 43 percent 5-on-5 expected goals share, so they're getting outplayed at even strength and need help there. Their goalies have saved 2.7 goals more than expected, which is holding the record up. Hunt's numbers say he won't fix that, so we'd treat him as a bottom-pair option, not a difference-maker.
